# Following the 302 returns the whole person, not the match stub

**Claim.** A client that follows the redirect never sees the `{vanId, status}` stub — it ends up on GET /people/{vanId} and receives the full record with 200. This only works if the client converts to GET, as fetch and browsers do; `curl -X POST -L` keeps the method and gets 411.

Applies to: `~1people~1find/post`

## Observed exchange

_A person to match, carrying enough identifiers to clear the threshold._

```http
(setup) POST /people/create

{
  "firstName": "Harriet",
  "lastName": "Kowalski-{scope}",
  "dateOfBirth": "1975-03-14",
  "emails": [
    {
      "email": "harriet.kowalski-{scope}@example.com"
    }
  ],
  "phones": [
    {
      "phoneNumber": "9075554242"
    }
  ],
  "addresses": [
    {
      "addressLine1": "742 Evergreen Terrace",
      "city": "Springfield",
      "stateOrProvince": "AK",
      "zipOrPostalCode": "99501"
    }
  ]
}

→ 201
  Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/100000001
{
  "vanId": 100000001,
  "status": "Stored"
}
```

_Same find as ever, but this client follows the redirect. The 200 below came from GET /people/{vanId} at the end of the chain, which is why it is a whole person._
